summary: Restoration pledges are chiefly EU-level: at least 20% each of EU land and sea areas should have restoration measures by 2030, and all ecosystems needing restoration should have them by 2050; the reported EU mitigation potential from rewetting and restoring peatlands and wetlands is 51–54 Mt CO2-eq/yr. Conservation centers on an EU LULUCF carbon-sink target of -310 Mt CO2-eq by 2030; Italy’s binding 2030 allocation, reported relative to 2016-2018, is -3,158 kt CO2eq. A combined restoration-conservation measure—ecologically appropriate reforestation and sustainable forest management—has a potential of 8–235 Mt CO2-eq/yr. Agriculture includes improved fertiliser-use efficiency to cut 19 Mt CO2-eq/yr. These figures are mainly EU-level commitments rather than Italian hectare goals. Forests cover 92,936 km² (30.9% of Italy), agriculture 158,061 km² (52.5%), and wetlands 234 km² (0.1%), but no class-specific national area allocation is given.
